cohort: The study included 3010 pregnant women who delivered in the urban-rural fringe areas of Guangzhou and Foshan, China in 2019.
finding: Among the 3010 participants, 59.70% experienced adverse pregnancy events (APEs), with factors such as Guangdong nativity, rural residency, age, pre-pregnancy BMI, male fetal sex, and cesarean delivery significantly associated with their occurrence.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was identified as a significant factor influencing the occurrence of adverse pregnancy events.
cross-section timing: Data was collected for pregnant women who delivered in 2019.
